rationale_evidence.statement: Sharper statement of the theory's incompleteness: it is not missing answers, it is missing a premise — 𝒪, what KnowledgeOS is obliged to be able to do, was never written down, and five CRITICAL gaps are its shadow; a theory of sufficient state cannot be evaluated without the operations it must be sufficient for.

rationale_evidence.anchor:
> *"Zero is computable, total and terminating over finite R, **RELATIVE to per-requirement
> evaluators**.
rationale_evidence.statement: Computational closure is assessed CONDITIONALLY CLOSED: everything executed and computable (membership, equality, StructuralValid, contradiction detection, supersession, replay, lineage, Zero — 8/8 tests) is computable only relative to per-requirement evaluators (Γ semantics, HumanAuthorization oracles) that are themselves not established; the theory is computable down to its oracles, and the oracles are where the epistemics live.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Five of the five remaining CRITICAL theoretical holes are the same object: Sigma. ... STEP 272 ... does not exist.
rationale_evidence.statement: All five remaining CRITICAL theoretical holes (G-06 Sigma>=5 axes, G-25 Unknown homeless, G-27 Insufficient missing, G-11 evidence layer no inputs, G-12 no empirical relational structure) converge on the single object Sigma, matching the corpus's own Step 271 s271.35 marking Sigma RED and s271.36 commissioning the non-existent Step 272 to derive it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: |lower bound (forced)| = 14        |upper bound (named ∪ forced)| = 18 ... NOT derivable: which of the 4 band members are mandatory -- NORMATIVE -> D-1
rationale_evidence.statement: O is bounded but not determined: a 14-element lower bound and an 18-element upper bound are both derivable with no human input, along with the five-class partition and congruence rule (independently re-derivable since congruence is a property of an algebra's operations on its carrier, so an operation reading H is not an operation on K); only membership of the 4-operation undetermined band in the mandatory set is not derivable, because 'mandatory' is a normative predicate that no corpus of descriptions can entail -- this is D-1.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 'Determine' / determination object absent | this pass | G5 | Determination != Decision stated 19x -- the operation is forced and unenumerated ... 'Q' epistemic sufficiency dropped | independent | G5 | typed at 42.40, absent from the ratified 6-tuple

rationale_evidence.anchor: The largest class is G5 -- PROMOTION. Eight of thirty-four gaps are constructions the corpus already contains and the canonical model never incorporated. Two of them are running, passing code.
rationale_evidence.statement: Headline finding: of 34 reconciled gaps, G5 (promotion) is the largest class at 8, versus G1 (genuine semantic gap) at only 5 (of which just 3 are irreducible: Qualify's body, AuthorityAct's type, U's algebra) and G10 (normative) at 4 -- everything else is promotion, repair, vocabulary or a normative choice.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The theory's deficit was never discovery. It was transcription: three successive reductions (ℛ 8→3 fields, status 10→2 values, DC 7→6 components) each discarded something the corpus had established, and each loss was later rediscovered as a fundamental gap.
rationale_evidence.statement: Final headline argument answering the mandate's central question: KnowledgeOS does NOT need a new theory -- of 34 reconciled gaps, 8 are promotions (two running/passing code), 6 are repairs of execution-falsified formulations, 5 are refinements, 4 are normative choices, exactly 1 requires innovation; the recurring failure pattern is three successive transcription reductions (relation 8-to-3 fields, status 10-to-2 values, a 7-to-6-component DC reduction), each of which discarded corpus-established content that was later independently rediscovered as a 'fundamental' gap.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Chain verdict: links 1-3 are canonically supported (partially); links 4 and 5 are severed; links 6-7 are partial; links 8-9 have no canonical content at all; link 10 is specified but unrun.
rationale_evidence.statement: A ten-link canonical implementation chain is built (Canonical Objects, Canonical State, Canonical Invariants, Canonical Operations, Canonical Transformations, Evidence, Authority/Governance, Persistence, Replay, Tests), each classified PARTIAL/BLOCKED/OPEN with governed-only provenance. Links 4 (Operations) and 5 (Transformations) are severed/blocked; 8 (Persistence) and 9 (Replay) have no canonical content; 10 (Tests) is specified (EG-05) but unexercised.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Therefore the minimum canonical contract is: Operation registry (membership + criterion + closure claim) └─ per operation: Precondition Postcondition Invariant-preservation obligations ... plus: State identity + equality rule
rationale_evidence.statement: The mandate's proposed seven-field operation-contract shape (Operation+Precondition+Postcondition+Invariant preservation+Evidence effect+Authority effect+Replay effect) is necessary but not sufficient; three further components are canon-forced: (i) a closed operation registry with a membership criterion, (ii) typed rejection/failure semantics, (iii) a state identity and equality rule -- because postconditions are undecidable without state equality and per-operation contracts are incomplete without a closure claim.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Ratify a closed operation registry with a membership criterion -- or explicitly rule that none exists yet and mark the implementation contract BLOCKED at that point.
rationale_evidence.statement: The single smallest decision that would unlock implementation is ratifying (or explicitly refusing) a closed operation registry with a membership criterion; this single act unblocks links 4 and 5 of the chain and, through them, pre/postconditions, invariant-preservation obligations, and replay effects. No broad gap-discovery pass is indicated because the gap is undecided (a governance act is missing), not under-analysed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: RECOMMENDED: D — THE OPERATION UNIVERSE DEPENDS ON AN UNRESOLVED PRIOR CANONICAL DECISION ... the test did not fail and did not merely run out of evidence: it succeeded, produced a well-defined family of six minimal registries, and in doing so identified precisely which prior decisions determine membership
rationale_evidence.statement: The document recommends terminal verdict D over the weaker B (six registries exist, computed) or C (none is fit for ratification) -- D holds that the operation universe's membership depends on unresolved prior canonical decisions (P-1..P-10), which is offered as the most informative and actionable framing since the test succeeded (did not fail, did not run out of evidence) and precisely identified which decisions gate membership, led by the typing of Reject.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Every bound in the method biases toward fewer registries and more necessary operations — that is, toward verdict A. A result that nevertheless finds multiplicity is therefore reported against the bias of its own method.
rationale_evidence.statement: Every declared modelling commitment (M1-M6, six constructed operations, depth/witness-size/budget bounds) is analysed for which direction it biases the conclusion, and every one biases toward fewer registries and more necessary operations (toward a false single-answer verdict A). Since the test nonetheless found genuine multiplicity (six registries, a nine-operation undetermined band) despite every bound working against finding multiplicity, the multiplicity result is reported as robust to its own method's bias -- strengthening confidence that it is not a search artefact.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 23 operation blocks covering 24 operations ... 253 commission cells ... RATIFIED-SOURCED 27 ... EXECUTED 24 ... PROPOSED 12 ... NORMATIVE DECISION REQUIRED 69 ... no operation has a complete canonical contract, and none can have one until P-8/P-9/P-10 of MINIMALITY-RESULT.md §5.3 are settled.
rationale_evidence.statement: A mechanically-verified contract-completion scorecard over 23 blocks (276 rows, 253 commission cells, no blank cells): 27 cells RATIFIED-SOURCED, 24 EXECUTED, 12 PROPOSED, 69 marked NORMATIVE-DECISION-REQUIRED (46 of which are the two universally-open fields, invariant obligations and failure semantics; the rest are operation-specific). Compared against the governed baseline (OPERATION-CONTRACT-GAP.md §B: 2 cells fully fixed, 9 partial, 88 empty across 9 capabilities), this represents substantial new grounding, but the honest overall verdict stated is that no operation has a complete canonical contract, and none can until three named prior canonical decisions (P-8 state equality, P-9 closed invariant register, P-10 typed rejection vocabulary) are settled.

K*, A∈K, K1=K2, and the Step 259/266 sufficiency and minimality results all inherit this gap. Resolution requires HUMAN DECISION D-1, after which the gaps below it become derivable [S1720]. Sharper statement of the theory's incompleteness: it is not missing answers, it is missing a premise — 𝒪, what KnowledgeOS is obliged to be able to do, was never written down, and five CRITICAL gaps are its shadow; a theory of sufficient state cannot be evaluated without the operations it must be sufficient for [S1721]. Reconciled gap register across all three tracks classifies most findings as G5 (promotion): the Determine operation/object, D_t, the R 8-tuple, the ten-status set, Q epistemic sufficiency, (W,Omega)/Identifiable, U(H) uncertainty carrier, and 𝒦=(K,H) are all corpus-present constructions the canonical model never incorporated [S1785]. Headline finding: of 34 reconciled gaps, G5 (promotion) is the largest class at 8, versus G1 (genuine semantic gap) at only 5 (of which just 3 are irreducible: Qualify's body, AuthorityAct's type, U's algebra) and G10 (normative) at 4 -- everything else is promotion, repair, vocabulary or a normative choice [S1785]. Final headline argument answering the mandate's central question: KnowledgeOS does NOT need a new theory -- of 34 reconciled gaps, 8 are promotions (two running/passing code), 6 are repairs of execution-falsified formulations, 5 are refinements, 4 are normative choices, exactly 1 requires innovation; the recurring failure pattern is three successive transcription reductions (relation 8-to-3 fields, status 10-to-2 values, a 7-to-6-component DC reduction), each of which discarded corpus-established content that was later independently rediscovered as a 'fundamental' gap [S1788]. A ten-link canonical implementation chain is built (Canonical Objects, Canonical State, Canonical Invariants, Canonical Operations, Canonical Transformations, Evidence, Authority/Governance, Persistence, Replay, Tests), each classified PARTIAL/BLOCKED/OPEN with governed-only provenance. Links 4 (Operations) and 5 (Transformations) are severed/blocked; 8 (Persistence) and 9 (Replay) have no canonical content; 10 (Tests) is specified (EG-05) but unexercised [S1965]. The mandate's proposed seven-field operation-contract shape (Operation+Precondition+Postcondition+Invariant preservation+Evidence effect+Authority effect+Replay effect) is necessary but not sufficient; three further components are canon-forced: (i) a closed operation registry with a membership criterion, (ii) typed rejection/failure semantics, (iii) a state identity and equality rule -- because postconditions are undecidable without state equality and per-operation contracts are incomplete without a closure claim [S1965]. The single smallest decision that would unlock implementation is ratifying (or explicitly refusing) a closed operation registry with a membership criterion; this single act unblocks links 4 and 5 of the chain and, through them, pre/postconditions, invariant-preservation obligations, and replay effects. No broad gap-discovery pass is indicated because the gap is undecided (a governance act is missing), not under-analysed [S1965]. The two operations the commission's T-3 task names as unreconciled against the executed algebra are Split and LinkEvidence; the script reports which sources name each [S1969]. The document recommends terminal verdict D over the weaker B (six registries exist, computed) or C (none is fit for ratification) -- D holds that the operation universe's membership depends on unresolved prior canonical decisions (P-1..P-10), which is offered as the most informative and actionable framing since the test succeeded (did not fail, did not run out of evidence) and precisely identified which decisions gate membership, led by the typing of Reject [S1976]. Every declared modelling commitment (M1-M6, six constructed operations, depth/witness-size/budget bounds) is analysed for which direction it biases the conclusion, and every one biases toward fewer registries and more necessary operations (toward a false single-answer verdict A).
